message.content:
**Answer**

The last common ancestor of lions (*Panthera leo*) and zebras (*Equus quagga*) is a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived during the early Paleogene (Paleocene–Eocene), roughly 60–70 million years ago. This ancestor belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which later split into the two major lineages that gave rise to the orders **Carnivora** (to which lions belong) and **Perissodactyla** (to which zebras belong). In other words, the common ancestor is a member of the Laurasiatherian stem group that predates the divergence of the carnivoran and perissodactyl lineages.
